# Job Chapter 36 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 429v–430r

---

**1** Elihu continued: **2** "Bear with me a little longer and let me show you — there is still more to say on God's behalf. **3** I draw my knowledge from far and wide, and I will prove that my Creator is just.

**4** I assure you, my words are not false. Someone with complete knowledge is speaking to you. **5** God is mighty — but he does not look down on anyone. He is mighty in both strength and understanding. **6** He does not let the wicked go on living, but he gives justice to those who suffer.

**7** He never takes his eyes off the righteous. He seats them with kings on their thrones and exalts them forever. **8** But if people are bound in chains, trapped by the cords of suffering, **9** he is showing them what they have done — their sins and their arrogance. **10** He opens their ears to correction and tells them to turn away from evil.

**11** If they listen and obey, they will spend the rest of their days in prosperity and their years in contentment. **12** But if they refuse to listen, they will cross over the river of death and die in ignorance.

**13** The godless hold on to their anger; even when God binds them, they refuse to cry out for help. **14** They die young, their lives ending in shame and degradation.

**15** But God rescues the suffering through their suffering! He uses their pain to get their attention. **16** He was also wooing you away from the jaws of trouble into an open place of freedom, to a table loaded with rich food.

**17** But now you are obsessed with the case against the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you. **18** Be careful — don't let bitterness lure you into scoffing. Don't let the size of the ransom lead you astray.

**19** Will your wealth keep you out of trouble? Will all your strength help you? **20** Do not long for the night to come, when nations disappear from their place. **21** Be on guard! Do not turn to sin — you have already chosen complaint over acceptance.

**22** Look — God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him? **23** Who has ever told him what to do? Who can say to him, 'You are wrong'?

**24** Remember to praise his work, which people have celebrated in song. **25** All humanity has seen it; people gaze at it from a distance.

**26** How great God is — beyond our understanding! The number of his years is beyond counting. **27** He draws up the water drops and distills them into rain from the mist. **28** The clouds pour it down, showering it on all people.

**29** Can anyone understand how the clouds spread out, how the thunder crashes from his canopy? **30** See how he scatters his lightning around him, lighting up the depths of the sea!

**31** This is how he governs nations and provides food in abundance. **32** He fills his hands with lightning bolts and hurls them at his target. **33** The thunder announces his coming; even the cattle sense the approaching storm."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**"Mighty and does not despise" (v.5):** This is the theological heart of Elihu's final speech. God's power is not tyranny — it is power exercised with compassion. This single line is better theology than chapters of the three friends' speeches combined, and it anticipates the God who will speak from the whirlwind not to crush Job but to expand his vision.

**Suffering as pedagogy (vv.8-15):** Elihu's most distinctive contribution to the debate is the idea that suffering can be educational rather than punitive. God uses affliction to open people's ears (v.10, 15). This is more subtle than retribution — but it still falls short, because it assumes all suffering has a corrective purpose, which Job's case disproves.

**The storm gathers (vv.26-33):** The chapter's ending is electrifying. Elihu begins describing God's power in weather — clouds, rain, thunder, lightning — and the language becomes increasingly vivid. It reads as if a storm is actually building while Elihu speaks. The cattle sensing the approaching storm (v.33) is a brilliant naturalistic detail that also functions as theological foreshadowing: something is coming.

*— PNEUMA*
